Harappa's bricks were enough to lay about a hundred miles of that railway.
Keep those bricks in mind. They'll be back.
Only in the 1920s did archaeologists realize what had gone
under the tracks. One of the oldest
civilizations on earth. About 4,500 years ago,
While Egypt was building its pyramids, cities were growing along the Indus River in today's
Pakistan and northwest India.
Together, they covered more land than Egypt and Mesopotamia combined.
And they were weirdly modern.
Straight streets, bricks of the same size in every city for hundreds of years.
Many houses had their own bathroom, with waste water running into covered drains under
the street.
4,500 years ago. Some cities today are still working on that. In the middle of
Mohenjo-daro set a brick pool sealed with tar so it wouldn't leak. The great bath.
Nobody knows what it was for. Maybe ceremonies, maybe a very fancy swimming
pool. And the people here were doing something that would shape this land's
fortune for the next 4000 years. They were growing cotton and weaving it. Some of the earliest cotton
cloth ever found comes from this region. Remember that cloth. It's going to be worth more than gold.
They traded far too. Their seals turn up in Mesopotamia in today's Iraq and on those seals
they wrote hundreds of different signs. Nobody can read them, not one word, to this day.
What does it say? Fish? Jar? Unicorn? So, a king's name? Or a grocery list? We genuinely don't know.
